title: Vice President
lead: The office embodies the Constitution's vision of ==continuity, balance and neutrality== — ensuring that neither the Executive nor Parliament ever faces a vacuum in authority. ==Read with MCN 45.==

items.title: Presiding Over Proceedings
bullets: Orderly conduct, regulating debate, discipline
==2018==: VP Naidu rejected the impeachment motion against ==CJI Dipak Misra== as ‘lacking merit’
==2023==: VP Dhankhar intervened to prevent disruptions during the ==women's reservation bill==

items.title: Interpreting Rules
bullets: ==2015==: Ansari permitted a calling-attention motion on rising intolerance despite government objection
==2023==: Dhankhar disallowed short-duration discussions citing ==Rule 267== — contested discretionary reach

items.title: Admissibility of Motions
bullets: ==2012==: Ansari admitted the ==FDI in retail== discussion despite government hesitation
==2023==: Dhankhar refused the ==Pegasus== motion under Rule 267

items.title: Casting Vote
bullets: Like the US VP in the Senate — rare in India due to party dominance
==1972==: VP Pathak's tie-breaking vote on the ==Payment of Bonus Bill==

items.title: Committee Powers
bullets: Nominates members to parliamentary committees
==2004==: Shekhawat ensured cross-party inclusion in the ==Ethics Committee== during the cash-for-query scandal

items.title: Decorum & Discipline
bullets: ==2021==: Naidu suspended ==12 Opposition MPs== in the Winter Session — criticised as excessive

items.title: Federal Balance
bullets: ==GST debate (2016)==: Ansari ensured TN and WB concerns were heard → ==compensation guarantees==

items.title: Debate Beyond Polarisation
bullets: Post ==26/11 (2008)==: Ansari promoted non-partisan national-security debate → consensus on revamping intelligence architecture

items.title: Constitutional & Ethical Custodian
bullets: ==2023==: Dhankhar publicly criticised the SC's basic-structure remarks — controversy over ==expected neutrality==

sections.title: Analysis of the Role as Chair

head: Issue
Explanation & impact
rows: Except when acting as President, no substantive executive or legislative authority.
Usually from the ruling party → RS neutrality may be compromised.
Heads no committee; no advisory or decision-making role in governance.
RS can function under the Deputy Chairman; presidential succession is a rare contingency.
Unlike the President, not elected by states → ==weaker federal legitimacy==.
Overshadowed by Leader of the House
Floor management sits elsewhere — VP's powers become ==procedural, not substantive==.

head: Feature
India
USA
UK
France
rows: National popular vote via the presidential ticket
No permanent VP; succession via President of Senate
President of Senate presides over joint sessions occasionally
Rarely acts; PM is executive head
Highly political — often a future presidential candidate

items.title: Neutrality & Legitimacy
bullets: ==Code of impartial conduct== for the Chair; suspend active party membership on assuming office (Speaker convention)
Consult Leader of the House and Leader of Opposition before disciplinary decisions
==Include State Legislatures in the electoral college== at lower weightage — makes the VP national, not merely parliamentary
Long-term: ==consensus candidate model== with pre-election all-party consultation

items.title: Capacity & Function
bullets: Ex-officio head/co-chair of ==Rules, Ethics and Privileges Committees==
Annual ==‘State of Rajya Sabha Report’== on productivity, disruptions, legislative quality
Defined ==advisory role== — a constitutional advisory council with President & PM; inter-House coordination during deadlocks
==Cooling-off suspensions== for repetitive disruption; accountability time before voting
A dedicated ==Parliamentary Research Cell== and structured training in procedure, comparative practice and conflict mediation

blocks.text: The strength of the Vice-President's office lies not in its powers but in the neutrality with which it is exercised — and restoring that spirit amid rising political polarisation is vital to preserve the dignity of parliamentary democracy.
